quote: allegiance is paid to the head of the Sringeri math
note: Stuart, South Canara Manual, quoted; Karadi Brahmans officiate. Also Servegara (vol 6).

quote: Formerly all the Medaras were Saivites, but many are at the present day Vaishnavites, and even the Vaishnavites worship Siva.
note: Packet heading 'Mayan' is a splitter error; entry is Meda, Medara (full text line 1531). Coorg mentioned.

quote: The Maravans bear Saivite sectarian marks, but also worship various minor deities
note: No maṭha named. Sivaganga is a zamindari/place, not the Śivagaṅgā pīṭha.

quote: The castemen themselves prefer the name Sivadvija or Saivite Brahman.
note: Ambalavasi temple priests of Saivite temples; social government rests with Nambutiris (smartavicharam, not a sect).

quote: Their high priest belongs to the Umayorubhagam mutt of Kumbakonam, and the North Travancore Vellalas recognise the Panantitta Gurukal as their spiritual adviser.
note: Non-Brahmin Saiva maṭha at Kumbakonam; second guru: Panantitta Gurukal (North Travancore). Vellalas divided into Saiva and Asaiva.

quote: A sub-division of Lingayat Kapus, named after the village of Nanukonda in the Kurnool district.
There are three matams, whereat the Nattukottai Chettis are initiated into their religion, at Patharakkudi (or Padanakkudi) and Kila for males, and Tulavur for females.
note: Fervent Saivites; Patharakkudi etc. are caste matams.

quote: The three groups became disciples of three different matams, viz., Tiruvarur, Kumbakonam, and Vanchium.
note: Origin legend (Hayavadana Rao, quoted); Kumbakonam here not shown to be the Kāmakoṭi seat. Earlier a group went to Conjeeveram and received matams.

quote: It is safe to say that the Nambutiris are Shaivas, but not to the exclusion of Vishnu.
note: Entry runs under packet heading 'Nambiyatiri' (splitter). Sectarian controversies tabooed; Sankaracharya credited with their anacharams.

quote: There were in the beginning two religious factions among the Nambutiris, the Vaishnavas or worshippers of Vishnu in his incarnation as a boar, and the Saivas
note: Traditional two sections; Saivas dominated.

quote: three of the most renowned of the disciples of Sankaracharya were Nambutiri Brahmans, who received their initiation into the sanyasasrama at the great sage's hands.
note: Tradition of three maṭhas founded by Nambutiri disciples of Śaṅkara; Thurston does not say the Nambutiris follow them as a sect. The Nambutiri 'Smarta' (smartavicharam judge) NOT coded.

quote: the sub-divisions of the Smarta caste, Vadama, Brihatcharanam, Ashtasahasram, Sanketi, etc., to which they belonged.
note: Some Nambutiris recall ancestors from Tamil Smarta (east coast) divisions; says nothing of a maṭha.

quote: being Smartas converted to the tenets of Sankaracharya.
note: Subramani Aiyar glossing Buchanan (Vishnu deity, Siva mark): 'equal reverence to both'. No maṭha named.

quote: They are both Saivites and Vaishnavites.
note: A section wears the lingam and follows Lingayetism (Silavanta).

quote: A curious mode of carrying the dead among the Namadari or Vaishnavite Nagarthas
note: Namadari (Vaishnavite) vs Sivachar (Saivite) sections; no intermarriage from Sivachar side.

quote: Vellalas who put on holy ash, in reference to certain Jains, who formerly became Saivites
note: Former Jains who became Saivites.

quote: They are for the most part Saivites, but some belong to the Vadagalai or Tengalai Vaishnava sects.
note: Vadagalai/Tengalai in part; Brahman Gurukkals officiate.

quote: The Oddes are in some places Vaishnavites, in others Saivites
note: Packet heading 'Madura' is a sub-heading of Odde (splitter).

quote: By religion they are both Saivites and Vaishnavites.
note: Aruva sept Saivite, Hatti sept Vaishnavite; some Saivites are Lingayats.

quote: The Padma Sales profess to be Vaishnavites, but some are Saivites.
note: Sadhu sept lingam-wearing Saivites; Satani officiates at funerals.

quote: The Paidis are Vaishnavites, and sing songs in praise of Rama during the month Karthika
meaning Vaishnavite, is a sub-division of Besthas, who, on ceremonial occasions, wear the Vaishnava sect mark.
The Pallans are nominally Saivites, but in reality devil worshippers
note: Nominal.

quote: They pretend to be followers of Siva, and always attend the Adi Amavasai ceremonies at Courtallum.
note: Packet heading 'Palissa (shield) Kollan' contains the Paliyan article.
